content.title: About
content.content: Trail mix with nuts is a blend of various nuts, dried fruits, and sometimes seeds, designed as a quick snack for travel or active outdoor activities. The mix of sweet, salty, and crunchy flavors provides a convenient source of energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Common mixes include almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, peanuts, and sometimes walnuts.
Dried fruits such as raisins, cranberries, or dried cherries add natural sweetness without added sugar.
Trail mix originated in the United States in the 1940s as a lightweight, nutrient‑dense snack for hikers.
Pumpkin and sunflower seeds are often added to boost zinc and magnesium content.
Some versions contain chocolate chips or yogurt coating for extra flavor variety.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Nuts provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: High in protein and fiber
items.content: The combination of nuts and dried fruit supplies plant protein and dietary fiber, promoting satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The mix contains magnesium, phosphorus, vitamin E, and antioxidants that aid metabolism and immunity.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from dried fruit quickly replenish glycogen stores, while fats offer sustained energy release.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Cashews and almonds are good sources of calcium and magnesium, important for bone tissue.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: The blend can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Nuts and dried fruits are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Dried fruits are naturally sweet; people monitoring blood sugar should choose unsweetened versions.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Whole nuts may pose a choking risk for young children; crushing them is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Trail mix is handy in single‑serve packets, as a snack during workouts, hikes, or at the office. It can be tossed into yogurt, oatmeal, or salads for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep it refrigerated to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
